videoReconGuideHeroText: Video reconstruction extracts frames, aligns cameras with COLMAP, and trains a static Gaussian Splat model using the pinned Brush CLI.
videoReconGuideBasicsText: Once the route, sampling behavior and target scenes are clear, the quality presets and custom parameters are much easier to choose.

route.title: Reconstruction route
route.text: ffmpeg / ffprobe decode the video, COLMAP aligns cameras, and Brush trains PLY models. Auto and Environment keep all points; Object applies a subject crop.

sampling.title: Frame sampling
sampling.text: Preset frames are the target sampling size. The system samples sparsely across the clip; longer videos do not automatically receive more detail coverage.

scene.title: Best scenes
scene.text: Static rooms, objects, exhibits and tabletop spaces work best. Crowds, screens, mirrors, transparent objects and blank walls reduce stability.

result.title: Output
result.text: Completed tasks appear in the model gallery for preview or PLY/SPZ download. Keeping intermediate files helps debug failures.

videoReconGuideShootText: Source quality sets the ceiling. Reconstruction prefers slow, stable, continuous footage with visible texture.

path.title: Move slowly, avoid sudden turns
path.text: Keep a steady walking speed and a continuous path so camera poses have enough overlap to track.

overlap.title: Keep viewpoints overlapping
overlap.text: Orbit objects by at least half a circle to a full circle. For rooms, make sure each area is seen from multiple angles.

light.title: Use stable lighting
light.text: Avoid exposure jumps, strong reflections and flicker. Even lighting is usually more reliable than dramatic contrast.

blur.title: Reduce motion and blur
blur.text: People, pets, moving plants, screen content and fast motion become noise and may produce floating fragments.

long.title: Split or customize long videos
long.text: Scanning a whole home is normal, but a 10-minute clip is better split by room, or run with custom frames and Sequential matching.

videoReconGuideParametersText: High quality is a good default for most clips. Use Custom when the video is long, detail is lacking, or VRAM is tight.

frames.title: Target frames
frames.text: Controls how many images are sampled from the full clip. Raise it for longer paths and broader coverage; COLMAP and training will take longer.

iterations.title: Training iterations
iterations.text: Controls the selected engine's training budget. More steps do not repair missing views or failed camera alignment.

downscale.title: Input downscale
downscale.text: 1x keeps the most detail and uses the most VRAM. 2x is the balanced default. 4x saves resources for path checks.

matching.title: COLMAP matching
matching.text: Sequential is designed for long walk-throughs. Exhaustive is more robust but slows down quickly as frame count grows.

resolution.title: Input resolution
resolution.text: Brush uses an actual long-edge pixel cap and does not enlarge smaller inputs.

videoReconGuideDependencyText: Check these baseline requirements first. Settings can refresh the local diagnostics result.

ffmpeg.title: ffmpeg / ffprobe
ffmpeg.text: Reads video metadata, extracts frames and builds thumbnails. These are required before any video task can start.

colmap.title: COLMAP
colmap.text: Handles feature matching and camera pose estimation. Failures here often point to poor overlap, blur or low texture.

gpu.title: GPU and drivers
gpu.text: An NVIDIA GPU and compatible driver are recommended. Brush provides its own GPU runtime; no additional Python video training environment is needed.

storage.title: Disk space
storage.text: Frames, the COLMAP database, training logs and temporary models use disk space. Long videos need extra cache room.

brush.title: Pinned Brush CLI
brush.text: Trains and exports Gaussian Splats. Use the fixed CLI build installed by Sharp GUI, which supports running without its editor window.

videoReconGuideSetupText: Once the requirements are clear, configure it manually from the README or let a local AI agent handle it.
videoReconGuideInstallTitle: Installation is covered in the README
videoReconGuideInstallText: The README explains how to install the pinned Brush CLI, native COLMAP, and ffmpeg/ffprobe.
videoReconGuideAgentTitle: You can also ask an AI agent
videoReconGuideAgentText: Useful when you do not want to debug PATH, CUDA, Python and external commands step by step. Give this prompt to a local AI coding agent.
videoReconGuideAgentPrompt: Inspect the Sharp GUI video reconstruction pipeline, system, GPU/driver and local tool paths. Install the pinned Brush CLI, native COLMAP and ffmpeg/ffprobe according to the README. Avoid unrelated code changes. Refresh the diagnostic API and verify using synthetic footage.

videoReconCustomIterationsHint: More iterations can refine detail, but each extra step costs time.
videoReconCustomMatchingHint: Sequential scales to long walk-throughs. Exhaustive is more robust for fewer frames but grows quickly.

videoReconCustomMaxResolutionHint: 640–3840 pixels. Images are capped at this long edge without enlarging smaller source frames. More pixels use more VRAM.

brush.preview: Start with 8,000 iterations and a 1600 px long-edge cap. Runtime depends on camera alignment, frame count and the scene.
brush.high: About 8 frames per second, 15,000 iterations and a 1920 px training cap. More frame coverage and camera features preserve detail.
brush.extreme: 30,000 iterations; resolution follows the VRAM budget. Higher settings use more time and memory, and cannot fix missing camera coverage.
brush.custom: Set frame count, iterations, the actual long-edge cap and COLMAP matching for this video.
